title: Natural science elective
description: A natural science course, such as biology, chemistry, geology, astronomy, or further physics, often with a laboratory.
notes: CU: additional natural science credits to reach 17 credits of physics and natural science.

title: Humanities and social sciences elective
description: A general education course in the humanities or social sciences, such as history, philosophy, literature, economics, psychology, or sociology.
notes: CU: chosen from the college-approved HSS electives (18 credits with the writing course).

title: Logic
description: A course in reasoning: critical thinking or symbolic logic. Students study how to analyze and evaluate arguments, and how to write and prove statements in a formal logical language.
notes: Choice slot: CU's PHIL 1440 or PHIL 2440. Official descriptions are in the CU catalog's PHIL pages, which were not saved.

title: Ethics
description: A course in ethics, such as ethical theory, contemporary social problems, or the ethics of computing and information technology. Students examine moral arguments and apply them to real cases.
notes: Choice slot: CU's PHIL, CSCI 2750, INFO, ENLP, or EHON options (see the row's options).

title: Computer science elective
description: An upper-level computer science course chosen by the student from an approved list, to deepen knowledge in an area of interest.
notes: CU: approved coursework bringing computer science credits to at least 58.

title: College-approved writing course
description: An upper-division writing course on technical and professional communication: writing reports, proposals, and other documents for technical and general audiences.
notes: CU: chosen from the college-approved writing courses.

title: Natural science sequence
description: A second laboratory science course in a two-course sequence, such as a second semester of physics with an experimental lab, general chemistry with lab, or introductory biology with lab.
notes: CU: physics, chemistry, or biology sequences (see the row notes).

title: Free elective
description: A course of the student's choice from any department, used to reach the total credits needed for the degree.
notes: CU: additional coursework to reach at least 128 credits.

title: Senior capstone I
description: The first semester of a two-semester senior capstone. Student teams plan and begin a substantial software or design project, often for an outside client, practicing requirements, design, and project management.
notes: Choice slot: CU's Software Engineering Project, Entrepreneurial Projects, Senior Thesis, or Multidisciplinary Design sequences. Official descriptions are in data/raw/colorado/ (courses-csci page).

title: Senior capstone II
description: The second semester of the senior capstone. Teams complete, test, and deliver their project and present the results.
notes: Choice slot: the second course of CU's capstone sequence. Official descriptions are in data/raw/colorado/ (courses-csci page).

title: Computer science core course (1 of 5)

Students take five courses from the list.
